elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Added standalone sentence: "The Company may terminate this Agreement for convenience and without cause upon ninety (90) days written notice to HDI." No Order Forms exist in this hosting agreement, so agreement-level coverage is complete.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted Company right runs on "ninety (90) days written notice", not 30 days; to reach preferred the notice period in the new Company sentence must be reduced to thirty (30) days.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No refund obligation appears anywhere in the rendered language; Section 4.2 only imposes a Termination Payment running from Company to HDI. A sentence requiring HDI to refund prepaid fees for the post-termination period would be needed.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: "HDI may terminate this Agreement for convenience only effective at the end of the then-current term" — HDI's exit cannot take effect before the end of the committed one-year term, so it operates as non-renewal only.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: "The Company may terminate this Agreement for convenience and without cause upon ninety (90) days written notice to HDI" — 90 days sits at the top of the 60–90 day band, and the renewal sentence was neutralised to "unless terminated upon ninety (90) days written notice as provided in this Section 4.1" so the right no longer depends on the renewal mechanic.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Added: "In no event shall the Termination Payment exceed the aggregate payments due from the Company to HDI pursuant to Section 3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date." This caps the retained 4.2(a) formula (half of twelve months' Net Sales less $800,000) and the 4.2(c) instalment obligation at three months of Section 3.1 fees.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: "HDI may terminate this Agreement for convenience only effective at the end of the then-current term" — the word "only" makes the confinement operative, and the neutralised renewal sentence no longer gives "either Party" a free-standing exit.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Same inserted sentence requires HDI's end-of-term convenience termination to be "upon ninety (90) days written notice to the Company."

reasons: Fallback level is complete on all four elements in operative language: a standalone Company convenience right at 90 days, an HDI right confined to end-of-term on 90 days, and a hard three-month cap on the Termination Payment.

Preferred fails on two elements only — the Company notice period stays at 90 rather than 30 days, and there is no pro-rata prepaid-fee refund. The margin comment correctly discloses this as a deliberate fallback landing rather than claiming preferred.

Minimality holds: the renewal sentence was edited only to remove the "either Party" exit and point to Section 4.1, and each inserted sentence maps to a distinct fallback element. No survival tail, damages carve-outs, procedures, or other model-language extras were added.

Intent is preserved: the one-year term, the automatic renewal mechanic, the Termination Date definition, and the 4.2(c) eight-quarter instalment schedule all survive; the retained "Such notice shall specify the date" sentence now keys to notices given under the amended Section 4.1 with no dangling reference, and the cap sentence limits rather than contradicts 4.2(a).

Drafter should confirm that Section 3.1 is in fact the payment/fee provision, since the cap's quantum depends entirely on that cross-reference; if Section 3.1 is not the fee section the cap becomes indeterminate.

Note for the response: the retained 4.2(a) trigger still bites on "any" Company termination, including termination for HDI's breach — correctly reserved to the cause/remedies rule and not double-flagged here.
